head: e95dfb42ed21df60e11e5f03e362befaf552a2ca
claim: A phone app that installs the released @byokit/accounts 0.31.0 can sign in to a MiniMax plan by user code with its own Web Crypto: the code shows, the account is kept as a ready plan and a question is answered through it; with no crypto the sign-in is refused before anything is sent.

steps.start: a fresh phone-shaped consumer app with no package and no account; the device has getRandomValues but no crypto.subtle, like React Native
steps: install the packed @byokit/accounts release tarball into the app
before: the published 0.30.0, installed the same way, reads both MiniMax plan routes as not ready on React Native
read minimax:code and minimax:code:cn on React Native: both ready, billed as the plan
start a MiniMax sign-in with no crypto passed: refused before anything is sent, naming the missing crypto
start it again with the app's own Web Crypto: the phone shows the code, the person approves it at the stand-in
the account is kept as a ready MiniMax plan and one question is answered through the plan token
steps.result: the released package signs a phone in to a MiniMax plan: code shown, account ready, answer "Hello Umer"; with no crypto it refuses before any request

verdicts.seen: I read all 11 capture lines plus the before-run lines. The installed package is @byokit/accounts@0.31.0. Both MiniMax routes (minimax:code and minimax:code:cn) show readiness ready and billing subscription. With no crypto, the sign-in is refused and requests sent 0 and accounts kept 0. With crypto, the phone shows code FIXTURE-MINIMAX-CODE, approve at the stand-in is true, PKCE uses SHA-256, the account is provider minimax, billing subscription, state ready, and the answer is 'Hello Umer (stop stop)' with 1 request to the plan API. The 0.30.0 before-run shows needs_host, which is the contrast. The outcome is shown. The outcome names no separate widths or frames, so parts and covers are empty.
